text: Source for Curlew-7 is written in Kotlin; no other language is allowed in its repository.
Bittern-2 reaches its retirement date on March 24, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
Bittern-2 was granted a budget of $795k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Curlew-7 has one owner, the Compass team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Swift-2 runs in the Cairo datacenter, next to its database.
The pager rotation for Avocet-4 is run by Gideon Nakamura; alerts page them first. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Kestrel-2, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Swift-2 is the Sprocket team. Nobody should assume the owner of Swift-2 applies to Kestrel-2, the owner differs.

Unlike Bittern-2, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Swift-2 is 2358. Nobody should assume the port of Swift-2 applies to Bittern-2, the port differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Siskin-4 enforces a rate limit of 1850 requests per minute per caller. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Siskin-4 was granted a budget of $4460k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.

Unlike Avocet-4, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Siskin-4 is Elixir. Nobody should assume the language of Siskin-4 applies to Avocet-4, the language differs. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Bittern-2, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Swift-2 is July 5, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Swift-2 applies to Bittern-2, the retirement date differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Unlike Kestrel-2, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Bittern-2 is the Tessera team. Nobody should assume the owner of Bittern-2 applies to Kestrel-2, the owner differs.
For Bittern-2 the port is 2162. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Avocet-4 listens on port 5825; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
All instances of Kestrel-2 live in the datacenter at Perth.
Finance fixed the budget of Curlew-7 at $385k, reviewed every quarter. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The retirement date for Kestrel-2 is February 4, 2029; after that day it stops serving.
Unlike Swift-2, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Kestrel-2 is the Compass team. Nobody should assume the owner of Kestrel-2 applies to Swift-2, the owner differs.
The retirement date for Avocet-4 is November 14, 2029; after that day it stops serving. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Curlew-7, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Siskin-4 is the Cairo datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Siskin-4 applies to Curlew-7, the datacenter differs.
Source for Avocet-4 is written in Swift; no other language is allowed in its repository.
Curlew-7 runs in the Perth datacenter, next to its database.
Avocet-4 was granted a budget of $3940k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Curlew-7, which is 2100 requests per minute. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Pages from Swift-2 land on the pager rotation of Umar Ekwueme before anyone else.
The pager rotation for Kestrel-2 is run by Celia Valdivia; alerts page them first. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Siskin-4 has one owner, the Ledger team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Bittern-2 enforces a rate limit of 4500 requests per minute per caller.
Kestrel-2 listens on port 7591; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
